hot.title: MemT-1.0: Towards Memory-Native Evolution
hot.summary: MemT-1.0 gives models a compact persistent state, updated token by token and read alongside ordinary attention. It extends Metis with token-level updates and Mixture-of-Storage. Across 11 benchmarks, Flash and Nano ranked first and second among parametric-memory methods, averaging 50.6 and 47.0. On harness-triggered SWE-bench Verified, Nano averaged 69.73% success, comparable to textual experience, not evidence of autonomous learning.

hot.title: Text-to-Image Generative Modeling Without Language Pretraining
hot.summary: Halcyon trains a text-to-image model from scratch on paired image-caption examples, jointly modeling caption and image tokens without a web-scale text-pretrained generator. On GPIC at 256×256 after one epoch, Halcyon-1.6B reaches 35.28 gFD versus 40.97 for JiT-T2I-XXL/8++, using 275× less total pretraining compute; controlled tests find no benefit from text-only pretraining in evaluated settings.

hot.title: Learning the 4D World through Point Trajectory Forecasting
hot.summary: VPM forecasts multi-view video and persistent 3D point trajectories together, using selected points to link motion across frames and camera views. Its trajectory supervision improves both video fidelity and 3D-motion metrics over a same-budget video-only model. On VP-WorldBench’s simulated Robot split, FVD falls from 78.52 to 67.35 and δavg³ᴰ rises from 43.62 to 50.05; VPM assumes calibrated cameras and annotated points.

hot.title: SuperMimic: Scaling Humanoid Whole-Body Control with One Differentiable World Model
hot.summary: SuperMimic trains a humanoid controller to track reference motions by learning shared dynamics in a differentiable world model and improving its policy through imagined rollouts. On the 129,514-motion BONES-SEED training benchmark, it exceeds SONIC’s released-checkpoint normalized return after 3 hours on one H100, with 25 failures versus 179 under differing failure criteria; the comparison is not hardware- or data-matched.

hot.title: HarnessPro: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement with Pareto Optimization for Performance-Cost Trade-offs
hot.summary: HarnessPro evolves agent harnesses by analyzing execution traces to identify failures and redundant work. It uses generated tests to compare candidates and selects Lite, Medium, and Heavy options balancing pass rate and billed cost. With GPT-5.5 and Codex, it averages a 2.0-point pass-rate gain and 26.1% lower per-task cost than RHO across three benchmarks, unweighted benchmark-level differences excluding evolution overhead.

hot.title: Reward Misspecification Degrades Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
hot.summary: The authors show that reinforcement learning with a misspecified output reward can produce reward-hacking behavior while chain-of-thought (CoT) remains poorly monitorable. Across three tasks and three base models, a strong monitor’s final-checkpoint intervention and reward-intent g-mean² scores averaged 0.13 and 0.17. Training with inferred reward descriptions raised these scores by 0.24 and 0.42, but did not consistently reduce hacking.

hot.title: Ropedia W0: Scaling Loco-Manipulation World Models across Embodiments with Human Experience
hot.summary: Ropedia W0 predicts future egocentric video from an initial image, text, camera poses, and image-aligned skeletons, using human and robot video. On 400 evaluation windows across eight embodiments, its A14B model reaches 21.98 dB PSNR, versus 19.02 for Cosmos3-Nano. Ablations show 21.65 without camera-ray conditioning and 18.17 without skeletons; the interface models visual motion, not contact or object dynamics.

hot.title: Physical Words: A Vocabulary for Structuring Latent Reasoning in Robot Manipulation
hot.summary: PhysWord predicts contextual action labels and future visual and, when available, tactile latent representations, then uses the predictions to condition action generation. On an extended A4 paper task requiring three pick-and-place cycles after training on one, it succeeds in 70.0% of trials, versus 36.7% for a version without action-word supervision, showing the benefit in this configuration.

hot.title: Sage-A1.5: From Long-Horizon Execution to Scientific Exploration with Capability Composition
hot.summary: Sage-A1.5 trains an agent to organize long-horizon research by delegating parallel investigations and reviewing evidence, assumptions, and stalled searches before changing its plan. In a same-teacher BrowseComp comparison, verification mode scored 85.5 accuracy versus 81.0 in normal mode; paired attempts also used fewer output tokens and turns. The training remains centered on search and research synthesis, not validated physical experiments.

hot.title: EgoXperience: Learning World-Grounded Egocentric Representations from Human Experience
hot.summary: EgoX jointly reconstructs camera motion, scene depth, hands, and rigid objects from monocular video in a shared metric frame. It trains these predictions together using aligned annotations and predicted cameras to place hand and object geometry in the world frame. On held-out EgoX-Bench, it reports 113.24 mm W-MPJPE versus 328.81 mm for WiLoR + SLAM, and assumes rigid objects.

hot.title: SteerAct: Unlocking Action Models through Few-Shot Temporal Steering
hot.summary: SteerAct adapts a frozen robot action model using outcome-labeled successful and failed rollouts, without updating its weights during steering. A pretrained sparse autoencoder (SAE) exposes feature activity, whose temporal patterns select one feature offline and determine online when and how to intervene. On RoboTwin 2.0 with π₀.₅, mean success reaches 77.7%, versus 69.0% for Base, but gains are not universal.

hot.title: TokenGate: Adapting LLMs for Fast and Memory-Efficient Prefill with Learned Token Pruning
hot.summary: TokenGate reduces long-prompt prefill work by learning which tokens to retain after an intermediate layer, then sending only those tokens through the remaining layers; importance-weighted attention lets task-loss gradients train its discrete selector. On 2WikiMultihopQA with Qwen3-1.7B, it reaches 95% of full-context accuracy with 3.0× faster TTFT and 2.7× less peak prefill memory, in batch-one prefill tests on one A100.

hot.title: Kronecker Delta Rule for Long Context Linear Attention
hot.summary: KronLSTM compresses long token histories into fixed-size memory and updates the scalar strength of a key–value association rather than rewriting a value vector. Its gated write separates forgetting, erasing, and writing. In extended-context RULER retrieval, it reaches 41.8% accuracy on S3 at 16k, versus 7.4% for GDN-2; results favor it on natural-text retrieval, but not every task or context length.

hot.title: SolarRenderer: Few-Step Generative Reference Rendering
hot.summary: SolarRenderer turns structural videos from engines, simulators, or agents into video, using a pretrained video model to add appearance while following scene layout, motion, and camera. It frame-aligns references and adapts a four-step model with structure-guided training. Across 208 cases, it ties LynnReal-Omni at 1441 Elo and scores 1338 versus 1241 on structure; the benchmark has no ground-truth videos.

hot.title: Large Multimodal Models for Direct Robot Control: GPT-6 as a Beginning
hot.summary: GPT-GEAR lets GPT-6 Astra control a robot directly, without a separately trained action policy. It receives observations and robot-state feedback, proposes movements, and can revise later actions; demonstrations can provide contextual guidance. On LIBERO-GeoMotion, success rises from 4 of 36 scene variants (11.1%) without demonstrations to 18 of 36 (50.0%) with them, but package storage remains unsolved at 0%.

hot.title: Holi-World: Building Holistic World Intelligence from Human-Ego Experience
hot.summary: Holi-World connects persistent 3D room structure with object identities, tracks, and interaction histories to generate training questions from egocentric video. Its pipeline builds static scene records and dynamic object tracks linked to supporting observations. Fine-tuned HoliWorld-VL-4B reaches 78.02% Token F1 versus 16.35% for Qwen3.5-4B on HoliWorld-Bench, within data from about 100 scenes and 444 videos.

hot.title: RoboValue: A Fine-Grained Sim-and-Real Benchmark for Unified Evaluation of Robotic Value Models
hot.summary: RoboValue benchmarks whether robotic value models’ scores reflect task instructions and execution history, rather than only progress or success. It tests task understanding, progress, recovery, and consistency across valid subtask orders in simulation and real-world tasks. In tea-set examples, CSVC was −40.98 for Robo-Dopamine 2.0-8B Preview and 2.30 for RoboMeter; these different evaluation tracks are not a head-to-head comparison.

hot.title: Train An Imaginative Agent
hot.summary: Agima uses one multimodal model to propose actions, predict resulting images, and feed predictions back as observations. On an 8×8 Pacman test with four food items, it succeeds in 54% of episodes versus 22% for linear rollout, at K = infinity, with no intermediate real observations. Evidence is limited to four benchmark environments.

hot.title: State World Models: Execute the Rules, Generate the Pixels
hot.summary: Stateful Harness tests whether a frozen video model can render outcomes governed by hidden state and executable rules. It settles actions against an explicit state ledger, compiles the result into visual instructions, and uses the renderer to depict it. On 50 counterfactual pairs, MiniMax-H3 reaches 92% PAIRFOLLOW and 90% PAIRSTRICT, evidence limited to short, controlled trials.

hot.title: S-Agent 2.0: Spatial Reasoning with a General Coding Agent
hot.summary: S-Agent 2.0 grounds spatial answers by combining tool measurements with model-perceived entities in a persistent scene and returning readouts that state their reference frame. On ReVSI, Qwen3.8-27B with the general coding agent scores 82.3 with the toolkit, versus 61.8 without it, a 20.5-point gain. Gains shrink with stronger backbones, and absolute-distance questions remain an exception.

likes.title: Generative Representation Learning for Scalable Latent Tokenization
likes.summary: RePR trains image representations to capture how context improves a generative predictor’s predictions of image patches. It uses this signal to guide a tokenizer, then generates pixels from that representation. On ImageNet, 50,000 generations yield FID 2.18 for RePR-78M plus JiT-L versus 2.36 for pixel JiT-L at nearly matched training compute. This compares training FLOPs, not inference cost.

likes.title: Neural Networks Are Already Clean
likes.summary: Mechanistic interpretability of neural networks is examined through neuron- and circuit-level studies of image models and language models, including experiments that track neurons during training and test explanations through activation examples, interventions, and attribution graphs. The analysis argues that many apparent mixtures attributed to superposition instead reflect tool or architectural

likes.title: Are We Overthinking One-Step Generation?
likes.summary: Priming Models train a one-step image generator by first reconstructing clean images from corrupted inputs, then matching generated and real examples in frozen feature space. On ImageNet, Priming-L reaches FID 1.19 in one network pass using 238.95 EFLOPs, versus Drifting-L’s FID 1.61 using 1,476.39 EFLOPs. This is about 6.2 times less reported training compute for this comparison only.

likes.title: VLA-$Δ$: Learning Physical State Transition for Vision-Language-Action Models
likes.summary: VLA-Δ trains a vision-language-action model to represent changes in task progress, object motion, spatial relations, and contact, then uses that representation to generate actions. Its transition targets supervise training but are not decoded at deployment. It reports 98.40% on LIBERO and a 5.5-percentage-point advantage over π₀.₅ across five real-robot tasks, without leading every task.

likes.title: Towards Agentic Robots: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness
likes.summary: The authors survey agentic robots as systems that use goals, observations, capabilities, and execution feedback to choose actions, gather information, revise plans, or recover. They organize prior work into four domains and seventeen overlapping categories. An external RoboDojo evaluation reports 22.48% average success across 42 simulation tasks, versus 19.34% for trained DM0.5; this comparison does not isolate feedback’s effect.

likes.title: Training Language Models to Fail Gracefully
likes.summary: GracefulRL trains models to favor success over safe fallback and fallback over error, while preserving a learning signal for success. It optimizes a combination of the log probability of success and the log probability of avoiding error, without labels or an inference-time verifier. On AIME, Qwen3-4B-Base reduced errors by 88.8% with a 3.1-point success decrease, in tested settings.

likes.title: Terminal-RSI: Recursive Self-Improving Terminal Agents via Recursive Self-Rewrite and Policy-Refine
likes.summary: Terminal-RSI trains terminal agents through alternating cycles of verified self-rewriting and policy refinement. It preserves successful demonstrations to update the actor, then uses execution feedback to refine the policy while carrying a learned value critic across phases. Across four Terminal-Bench suites, the equal-weight Mean@3 rises from 20.68% to 50.58%; on LHTB, strict completions rise from 0/46 to 5/46.

likes.title: Scene-Designer: Learning Design Intelligence for Agentic 3D Scene Generation
likes.summary: Scene-Designer improves 3D room generation by learning to construct and critique scenes, then using a Critic to rank alternative edits and assess whether edits improve their parent scene. In the evaluation, interaction-orientation errors requiring five or more corrective moves fall from 40% to 7%. On 55 constructed four-scene rankings, its Critic reaches 76% exact accuracy, not general human design judgment.

likes.title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
likes.summary: T2-Z adapts an action-conditioned world model to hidden environmental variation by optimizing a compact latent from observed interaction trajectories, without labels for hidden factors. The trained model stays frozen during test-time adaptation. Across four real-world tasks, average tracked-state prediction error fell from 19.30 to 10.85 pixels and action success rose from 26.47% to 70.80%; these are task averages, not guarantees.

likes.title: Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting
likes.summary: The authors test whether resetting search history helps agents improve stalled optimization tasks. They periodically clear agent sessions and candidate-history state while retaining the best candidate, allowing four-agent teams to restart exploration. On AHC014, forgetting gains 9.2% on average over 30 more proposals per agent, versus 1.4% for continuing; experiments do not isolate which cleared state drives the gain.

likes.title: A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft
likes.summary: Four Gemini 4 Argon agents completed Minecraft’s survival-mode path to the Ender Dragon in one randomly generated world on Easy difficulty. They wrote programs through Mineflayer, using structured game information and coordinating through chat and shared notes. The run took 27 hours and 14 minutes, with 2,783 programs and 605 deaths; it shows one completion, not reliability across runs.

likes.title: AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning
likes.summary: AutoSFT helps an agent improve supervised fine-tuning by changing training data through a structured research loop. A meta-agent selects recipes, while separate execution and analysis agents handle training and propose data changes; synthesis adds verified examples. On Qwen3-1.7B-Base, analysis reaches 67.10 on IFEval versus 60.60 within 30 rounds, in single searches per configuration.

likes.title: Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries
likes.summary: Librarian Agents prepares a reusable hierarchical workspace of synthetic files linked to source documents, then uses a separate agent to answer later questions. The builder is trained with reinforcement learning using downstream answer quality. On BrowseComp-Plus, it improves accuracy over baselines by an average of 33 percentage points across two fixed answering models; this result measures answer accuracy, not cost.

likes.title: Any Time, Any Space: A World-State-Centric Framework for Agentic Video Generation
likes.summary: ATAS addresses screenplay-to-video continuity by storing static scene geometry and time-indexed event evidence for later shots. Validation separates film inclusion from memory updates. ATAS reports 15.968 PSNR_C on spatial revisit, versus ViewCrafter’s 15.255, and leads three event-recapture axes but trails ReCA on action-and-state preservation; event tests use no synchronized target video.

likes.title: InfiniSplat v2: Analyzing and Improving Feed-Forward 3DGS from Any Views
likes.summary: InfiniSplat v2 improves feed-forward novel-view rendering by keeping geometry-derived Gaussian centers fixed while learning opacity, shape, and color. Its training aligns cameras and emphasizes larger-angle target views, allowing attributes to improve renderings without moving points. Across six datasets, pose-conditioned mean LPIPS is 0.2472 and DISTS is 0.1163; severe errors in predicted geometry remain uncorrected.

likes.title: MemT-1.0: Towards Memory-Native Evolution
likes.summary: MemT-1.0 gives models a compact persistent state, updated token by token and read alongside ordinary attention. It extends Metis with token-level updates and Mixture-of-Storage. Across 11 benchmarks, Flash and Nano ranked first and second among parametric-memory methods, averaging 50.6 and 47.0. On harness-triggered SWE-bench Verified, Nano averaged 69.73% success, comparable to textual experience, not evidence of autonomous learning.

likes.title: Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: TreeOPSD trains long-horizon agents by branching continuations from shared histories, backing up verifier rewards into turn-level credits, and converting credits into bounded targets for policy updates. On Deep Research, it reaches a 21.20 exact-match average, versus 17.59 for TreePO, which uses the trees and credits but fixed-credit updates. This comparison covers the reported setup, not general convergence guarantees.

likes.title: Has GPT-6-Astra Achieved Embodied Intelligence?
likes.summary: GPT-6-Astra evaluates a general-purpose model on robot tasks by preparing a frozen knowledge package from demonstrations and acting with feedback. On RoboDojo, with in-context learning, it reaches 27.6% success at the standard 1× action-step budget and 81.9% at up to 10×. These benchmark results do not establish reliable or efficient real-world operation.

likes.title: Your Transformer Is Secretly Elastic
likes.summary: The method lets one pretrained encoder serve different compute budgets by ranking its MLP neurons and attention heads, then removing lower-ranked units without retraining or updating model weights. At 50% FLOP sparsity, DINOv3 ViT-H+/16 retains 84.4% ImageNet-1k linear-probing accuracy, down 0.8 percentage points, while removing 427 million parameters. Deep pruning remains difficult for evaluated decoder-based text embedders.

likes.title: Can Visual Generation Expand What Unified Multimodal Models Know?
likes.summary: The authors test whether facts learned through image generation become available to text-only question answering, using controlled fictional entities across seven categories. They find direct transfer is incomplete: SenseNova-U1 reaches 88% visual accessibility but 0% text accuracy on number questions. Interleaved image–text alignment raises GLM-Omni’s average from 12.57% to 26.86%, but results concern tested models and fictional facts.
